title: Table Configuration
description: A data table widget for displaying structured information in rows and columns. Use this widget to present lists, records, or any tabular data with customizable column types and formatting. Supports multiple column types: plain text, numbers with precision control, timestamps with format parsing, state indicators with color mapping, boolean values, clickable buttons with links, images, and edit buttons that hand a row's key to a form or another widget on the page through a URL parameter. Features include a configurable sort order, column width control, cell styling, horizontal overflow for wide tables, and header/cell separators.

aiSelection.dataShape: Rows and columns. Each columns[] entry binds one column of the source data and declares how to render it — string, number with precision, timestamp with format, boolean, state with a colour map, image, or a clickable button with a link. The row count is whatever the query returns. An 'edit' column shows one icon button per row: its values are the record key, and a click writes that key into the page URL under styling.parameterKey, so a widget-form opening on that parameter, or any widget filtering on it, shows the clicked record.
useWhen: The user needs to read individual records — event logs, device inventories, order lists, alarm histories — sorted by any columns (columns[].sortDirection).
More than two or three fields per row matter, so no chart can carry them all.
Exact values matter more than trends or comparisons.
Each row should offer a link or action of its own (a column of type 'button').

Each row needs an edit or open action that hands the record to another widget on the page — a column of type 'edit' with styling.parameterKey, next to a widget-form opening on that parameter or a detail widget bound with a Parameter filter on that key.
notFor: Spotting a trend, comparing magnitudes, or seeing a distribution — use widget-linechart; a table makes the reader do the work a chart does for them.
One number that matters more than the rest — use widget-value, or widget-gauge to read it against a range.

Shares of a total — use widget-doughnut when the parts are a fixed set that arrive as columns of one row (or as one value each); when the parts are rows of the result (one row per cause or program), use widget-linechart with dataseries[].type: 'bar'.
Text written by hand rather than queried — use widget-markdown.
Entering or changing a record's fields — use widget-form; an 'edit' column only selects the record for a form on the same page.

title.title: Title
title.description: The main heading displayed above the table. Use to describe the data being shown (e.g., 'Device Status', 'Recent Events', 'Inventory List').

subTitle.title: Subtitle
subTitle.description: Secondary text displayed below the title. Use for additional context like filters applied, time range, or data source.

horizontalOverflow.title: Enable Horizontal Overflow
horizontalOverflow.description: When enabled, table can scroll horizontally if columns exceed container width. Disable to force columns to fit within the available space. Enable for tables with many columns or fixed-width columns.

styling.title: Table Styling
styling.description: Global styling options that apply to the entire table.

headerFontSize.title: Header Font Size
headerFontSize.description: CSS font size for column headers (e.g., '14px', '0.9rem'). Controls the size of text in the table header row.

columnSeparators.title: Show Column Separators
columnSeparators.description: Display vertical lines between columns. Enable for clearer column distinction in dense tables, disable for a cleaner minimal look.

cellPaddingHorizontal.title: Cell Padding Horizontal
cellPaddingHorizontal.description: Left and right padding inside cells. CSS value like '8px', '1rem', or '0.5em'. Increase for more spacious cells, decrease for compact display.

cellPaddingVertical.title: Cell Padding Vertical
cellPaddingVertical.description: Top and bottom padding inside cells. CSS value like '8px', '1rem', or '0.5em'. Affects row height and text breathing room.

columns.title: Column Definitions
columns.description: Configure each column's header, data type, values, and styling. The order of columns here determines their display order in the table. Each column binds its values to a data source.

header.title: Header Label
header.description: The text displayed in the column header. Should clearly identify the data (e.g., 'Device Name', 'Status', 'Last Updated').

type.title: Column Type
type.description: Determines how cell values are rendered: 'string' for plain text, 'number' for numeric values with precision, 'boolean' for true/false display, 'state' for colored status indicators, 'timestamp' for formatted dates, 'button' for clickable actions, 'image' for displaying images, 'edit' for an icon button that writes the row's value (its record key) into a URL parameter, so a form that opens on that parameter, or any widget filtering on it, shows that record.

values.title: Values
values.description: The data values for this column. Each entry corresponds to a table row. Bind to a data source column to populate dynamically.

value.title: Display Value
value.description: The cell value to display. For images, this is the image URL. For buttons, this is the button label. For edit columns, this is the record key the button sends as the URL parameter; it is not displayed. For other types, this is the raw value to be formatted according to column type.

link.title: Link URL
link.description: Link of a button or image column, opened when the button or image is clicked. An absolute URL (with a scheme, such as https://example.com) opens in a new tab; a path without a scheme, such as /machines/press-1, opens that board page in place. Leave it empty for no link.

sortDirection.title: Sort
sortDirection.description: Sorts the table's rows by this column. 'asc' puts the smallest number, the earliest timestamp, false, the first state of the State Map (unlisted states after the listed ones, alphabetically) or text from A first; 'desc' reverses it. Empty cells always come last. Sort the timestamp column 'desc' to show the newest rows first; without a sort, rows show in the order the data arrives, oldest first. Viewers can still click a header to sort by that column; clicking it a third time restores this sort.

sortPriority.title: Sort Priority
sortPriority.description: Which sorted column counts first when several are sorted: 1 sorts first, 2 orders the rows that tie on it, and so on. Sorted columns without a priority come after those with one, in column order. Leave it empty when only one column is sorted.

styling.title: Styling
styling.description: Type-specific settings and visual styling for this column. Settings depend on the column type.

parameterKey.title: URL Parameter Key
parameterKey.description: For 'edit' columns: the URL parameter the button sets to the cell's value, such as 'edit'. Required: without it the button is shown disabled. Use the same name as the Open on URL parameter setting of the form, or the Parameter filter of the widgets, on this page that should show the clicked record.

iconName.title: Icon
iconName.description: For 'edit' columns: the Material Symbols icon name shown on the button, such as 'edit', 'open_in_new', 'visibility' or 'tune'. Empty means 'edit' (a pen).

timestampParseFormat.title: Timestamp Parse Format
timestampParseFormat.description: Format string for parsing input timestamp values using Unicode LDML standard (e.g., 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS'). Leave empty if timestamps are Unix epoch milliseconds (JavaScript timestamps).

timestampFormat.title: Timestamp Display Format
timestampFormat.description: Format string for displaying timestamps using Unicode LDML standard. Examples: 'yyyy-MM-dd' for date only, 'HH:mm:ss' for time only, 'MMM d, yyyy h:mm a' for friendly format. Leave empty for ISO 8601 format.

precision.title: Number Precision
precision.description: Number of decimal places for numeric columns. 0 for whole numbers, 1-3 for measurements. Only applies when column type is 'number'.

stateMap.title: State Map
stateMap.description: Maps state values to colors for 'state' type columns. Format: alternating value-color pairs like "'ONLINE': 'green', 'DISCONNECTED': 'red', 'PENDING': 'orange'". Values not in the map use default styling.

width.title: Column Width
width.description: Fixed width for this column. CSS value like '100px', '20%', or 'auto'. Use fixed widths for consistent layout or 'auto' to size based on content.

fontSize.title: Font Size
fontSize.description: CSS font size for cells in this column (e.g., '14px', '0.9rem'). Overrides the default table font size for this column only.

fontWeight.title: Font Weight
fontWeight.description: Numeric font weight for this column. 100-300 for light, 400 for normal, 700-900 for bold. Use bold (700+) for important columns.

color.title: Font Color
color.description: Text color for cells in this column. Use the color picker or enter a CSS color value. Overrides theme color for this column.

border.title: Cell Border
border.description: CSS border for cells in this column. Format: 'width style color' (e.g., '1px solid red', '2px dashed #333'). Useful for visual emphasis on specific columns.
